content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: SEV2 1 MarinerTech (customer-id: mnt-42) reporting dramatic KV prefix hit-rate collapse for prefix 'nav/' on dedicated pool dp-21. Alert: kv.prefix.hitrate.nav/ < 3% (threshold 55%)  elevated tail latency and error rate. Escalation to oncall maria-oncall.

maria-oncall: ack, I'm on. Brief? any signs of infra failure?

incident-bot: Recent signals:
- kv.prefix.hitrate (mnt-42/nav/) dropped from ~90% to 1.9% at 2026-03-15T13:02Z
- dp-21 leader logs show prefetch OOMs and mass evictions
- tenant traces show 500/503 ~15/min for nav/ routed requests
- no node reboots, GPUs healthy, autoscaler stable

leo-sre: joining. initial suspicion: cache pollution from a large prefix ingestion job (customer-side) triggering prefetch and then eviction cascade.

anya-runtime: pulling dp-21 runtime traces and prefetch metrics.

anya-runtime: raw log snippet:
```
2026-03-15T13:01:48Z dp-21 prefetch:init prefix=nav/ user=mnt-42 candidate_keys=1.2m
2026-03-15T13:01:55Z dp-21 kv.eviction.rate=120k/min
2026-03-15T13:01:55Z dp-21 cache_hitrate(mnt-42/nav/)=1.9%
2026-03-15T13:02:01Z prefetch:batch.assemble OOM heap=23.9GB
```

leo-sre: confirmed OOM -> eviction spike -> hit-rate collapse. Options: (A) disable prefetch for mnt-42 (fast), (B) increase kv_slot/quota for tenant (safer but needs capacity), (C) throttling large prefix writes at edge, (D) move tenant to isolated warm-pool.

maria-oncall: step 1 disable prefetch for prefix 'nav/' only if we can target prefix-specific toggle. Avoid full restart.

anya-runtime: we have per-tenant+prefix prefetch toggle. Executing now.

anya-runtime: command run:
```bash
redwoodctl kv set --tenant mnt-42 --pool dp-21 --prefix nav/ --prefetch disabled
# OK: prefetch disabled for mnt-42 nav/ on dp-21
```

(20s) anya-runtime: cache_hitrate -> 12% and evictions down to 8k/min. tail latency improving.

olivia-cs: looped in AM Ravi and product Sam. Ravi, please prepare a short note to MarinerTech.

ravi-am: drafting: "We're seeing cache instability affecting nav/ traffic. We've disabled automated prefetch for that prefix and applied temporary write-throttles. We're monitoring and will update within 30 minutes with next steps." Send?

olivia-cs: send now. include expected impact window.

ravi-am: sent at 13:10Z. customer acknowledged and flagged urgent partner integration tests are impacted.

sam-prod: we should throttle writes for nav/ to avoid reinjection. Can we apply a soft write rate limit of 40r/s and block huge batch inserts?

anya-runtime: can do per-prefix write throttle. Applying 40r/s and blocking >1000-key batch imports for 30m.

anya-runtime: commands:
```bash
redwoodctl kv throttle --tenant mnt-42 --prefix nav/ --writes 40/s --scope dp-21
redwoodctl kv control --tenant mnt-42 --prefix nav/ --max_batch_keys 1000 --duration 30m
```

leo-sre: good. also scheduling an asynchronous compaction to reclaim memory fragmentation once steady. Will run low-prio compaction on dp-21 leader nodes in 10m.

(5m) anya-runtime: compaction started (low priority). watching heap and GC.

(7m) anya-runtime: cache_hitrate now 37% -> 63% after compaction progress. error rate down to baseline (~1/min). Severity to SEV3 at 13:28Z.

maria-oncall: nice. move to medium-term mitigations: increase tenant kv_slots temporarily while we analyze access patterns, and plan to add tenant-level prefetch memory cap. Sam can you own product side of cap spec?

sam-prod: I'll draft spec. target: cap prefetch memory to 10% of tenant pool assignment, with backpressure and metrics.

olivia-cs: customer asked whether this was caused by an internal job. They will check on their side and share logs for the 13:00Z window.

leo-sre: taking heap profiles & prefetch traces saved to /private/incident_artifacts/1769056789/ for RCA.

maria-oncall: filing immediate follow-ups: INF-2099 "Tenant prefetch memory cap + prefix-level soft-throttles" assigned to anya-runtime and chris-eng. Also add runbook update for oncall.

chris-eng: noted. will look at adding defensive limits in runtime and safer defaults for dedicated pools.

ravi-am: customer update sent at 13:25Z: "Mitigations applied (prefetch disabled for nav/, write throttles). Performance improving; we will coordinate a deeper review and preventive config changes."

maria-oncall: handoff plan: I'll keep monitoring for 30m and then hand to leo-sre for daytime triage. Keep prefetch disabled for nav/ until compaction + 1h observation. Keep write throttle for 2h.

anya-runtime: exported trace bundles and heapdump: /private/incident_artifacts/1769056789/heaps/ and /traces/. Uploaded to internal dashboard link: https://console.redwood.internal/incidents/1769056789

(13:52Z) leo-sre: taking over monitoring. setting a muted alert for noisy eviction spikes but keeping the hit-rate threshold active.

olivia-cs: customer replied: "Thanks, this aligns with our deploys at that time. We'll coordinate changes and avoid big backfills during your maintenance window."

maria-oncall: final notes for handoff: keep throttles and prefetch toggle in place until product/eng ship prefetch memory cap. Postmortem owners: leo-sre (ops timeline), anya-runtime (runtime traces), sam-prod (product spec), chris-eng (runtime safety). Severity: downgraded to SEV4 for tracking.

incident-bot: Incident note recorded: mitigations applied: prefix-prefetch disabled, write throttle 40r/s, batch limit 1000, compaction run. Status: recovering/stabilized.

ravi-am: scheduling post-incident call with MarinerTech at 16:00Z today for RCA and next steps.

sam-prod: filed ticket INF-2099 and added acceptance criteria: metrics guardrails, tenant memory cap, admin toggles, and migration plan for heavy prefixes.

maria-oncall: closing paging loop. thanks team. if regression, escalate via pager.

leo-sre: noted. will produce timeline and initial RCA draft by EOD.

olivia-cs: adding incident summary to customer record.

(14:05Z) marinertech-rep (via email): "Appreciate the quick response. Please include mitigation steps in the RCA."

maria-oncall: will do. end of thread.
